sources_quoted.quote: Dealing {{as|physical damage}} to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks.
sources_quoted.used_for: Carve is a TARGET-SIDE armor-reduction debuff (benefits every attacker's physical damage, not just the holder's); hard cap 30% armor reduction.

sources_quoted.quote: After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]. If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources ({{fd|1.5}} second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).
sources_quoted.used_for: Expose Weakness is an explicit ALL-SOURCES incoming-damage amplifier on the target: 8% (melee) / 5% (ranged). In a coupled roster it amplifies every ally's damage.

sources_quoted.quote: m(R) = 100 / (100 + R)   (apply_resistance, resistance.py) ... post = raw * m(R)
sources_quoted.used_for: Damage-derived healing is linear in post-mitigation damage, so heal ratio = amp x (100+R_old)/(100+R_new).

sources_quoted.source: docs/math-foundations.md, Sec 2.3 item 2 (Black Cleaver average stacks)
sources_quoted.quote: the established model uses a fixed `0.8*max_stacks` constant (with a `hits/2` short-fight branch). Under the engine's own ordering convention ... the exact Cesaro mean of the capped ramp `min(k, C)` over `h` hits is `C - C(C-1)/(2h)` for `h >= C`
sources_quoted.used_for: Feasible per-fight average stack count: 4.00 stacks (24% reduction) at h=10, 4.50 (27%) at h=20, 4.82 (28.9%) at h=56, asymptote 5 (30%).

sources_quoted.source: data/champions.json -> Aatrox, abilities.E 'Umbral Dash' effect text (archetype of the damage-derived heal family this leaf belongs to)
sources_quoted.quote: Passive: Aatrox heals for 16% (+ 1.1% per 100 bonus health) of non-persistent post-mitigation damage he deals against enemy champions.
sources_quoted.used_for: Confirms the engine's damage-derived heals are a fixed fraction of POST-MITIGATION damage, i.e. proportional to m(R) and to any incoming-damage amplifier on the target.

sources_quoted.quote: formula: E passive heals 16% of post-mitigation ability damage (no bonus health), x2.0 while R ... Q 863.7 x 0.16 x 2.0 = 276.4
sources_quoted.used_for: Calibration: reproduced independently (Aatrox lvl18 AD 145 x 1.4 R3 = 203; Q 3-cast sweetspot raw = 459.375 + 5.90625 x 203 = 1658.3; Ahri lvl18 armor 92 -> x100/192 = 863.7; x0.32 = 276.4). Confirms the heal-vs-mitigation chain used below is the engine's real semantics, and that heals of this magnitude (260-320) are the expected scale for this family.

sources_quoted.used_for: Bounds the target armor A that any roster damage instance is mitigated by.

independent_computation.step_1_what_the_leaf_is: applied_amount on a healing event is the post-modifier heal actually applied (the corpus's grievous entry shows the sibling fields raw / applied / factor). No Grievous Wounds source exists in a Black-Cleaver+Bloodsong roster, and no sourced healing-reduction factor equals the observed change, so the change must come from the heal's raw amount, i.e. from the damage instance that generated it.
independent_computation.step_3_model: For every damage-derived heal in the engine, heal = k x post_mitigation_damage, k constant within one event. Hence ratio = amp x (100 + A) / (100 + A(1 - x)), where A = target armor before Carve, x = fractional armor reduction applied, amp = Expose Weakness incoming-damage amplifier (1.00, 1.05 or 1.08).

step_5_feasibility_against_sourced_caps.carve_cap: 0.30 (5 stacks x 6%), per the cached wiki text
step_5_feasibility_against_sourced_caps.carve_alone: INFEASIBLE for every level-18 champion in the cache: the required reduction is 0.307-0.365, above the 30% hard cap. So the observed jump cannot be Carve alone.
step_5_feasibility_against_sourced_caps.carve_plus_expose_weakness: FEASIBLE across the whole armor range: 0.19-0.28 required, all strictly inside the 30% cap and inside the average-stack band the math doc derives (0.24 at h=10 hits, 0.27 at h=20, 0.289 at h=56).

forward_check.comment: 4.5 average Carve stacks (Cesaro mean at h=20) + ranged Expose Weakness -> 315.7 vs golden 316.1 (0.1%)

independent_computation.step_6_conclusion: 261.8 is exactly the value obtained when NEITHER target-side debuff reaches this damage instance (amp = 1.00, x = 0). 316.1 sits in the middle of the band produced by applying both sourced debuffs at legal magnitudes (Carve 19-28% effective armor reduction, Expose Weakness 5-8%). Both debuffs are, per the quoted wiki text, inflicted ON THE TARGET and apply to damage 'from all sources' - so in a coupled roster every member's damage, and therefore every damage-derived heal, must carry them. The 55th healing event is deep in a long fight, where Carve is at or near full stacks (Cesaro mean 4.82 of 5 at h=56), so the near-cap reduction implied by 316.1 is exactly what the model predicts at that point in the timeline.

what_i_could_not_verify: The scenario's roster (champions, levels, ranks, full item sets, target identity) is not in data/ or docs/math-foundations.md, so the leaf could not be recomputed to the decimal - only bounded.
Which of the two debuffs (or both) the change actually restored; the arithmetic only shows that Carve alone is insufficient and Carve+Expose Weakness is sufficient.

Whether healing_events[] re-indexed between the two runs (an index-keyed leaf can compare two different events). If the event list length changed, this leaf's diff is a labelling artifact rather than a value change - worth confirming against the sibling leaves' shape.
flags_for_parent: If the engine models Expose Weakness at 8% for a RANGED Bloodsong holder, that is a data mismatch: the cached branch text is {{rd|8%|5%}} (melee/ranged split).

docs/math-foundations.md Sec 2.3 recommends replacing the 0.8*max_stacks Black Cleaver constant with the exact Cesaro mean C - C(C-1)/(2h). At h=56 hits the two differ by 4.8 percentage points of armor reduction (24.0% vs 28.9%), i.e. ~2-3% on this heal - large enough to matter for the last digit but far too small to explain the 20.74% diff on its own.
